confirmed: Read the complete markdown conversion and the entire one-page PDF, including the diagram and all plots; there are no additional PDF pages or appendices. The title and three authors match the form (PDF p. 1, title block).

source.version correctly identifies a one-page poster rather than a journal article; ISCOP 2026 is identified by the retrieval URL/filename, while the poster face itself has no displayed date or conference name. No supplement is referenced (PDF p. 1, entire poster; retrieval source URL).

Both task groups use solo rounds 1-3 followed by collaborative rounds 4-6, with AUT and SFT before and after HAICCO. No random assignment of AI assistance or randomized condition order is reported; quasi_people, observational context, and core=no are supported (PDF p. 1, HAICCO text and Study design diagram).
FAT: 100 completers, 60.0% female, mean age 43.40 years, SD 13.40 years. These are people, not word chains, ideas, or ratings (PDF p. 1, Participants panel).

DAT: 101 completers, 48.5% female, mean age 45.90 years, SD 12.80 years. These are people, and repeating solo/collaborative phases does not add independent participants (PDF p. 1, Participants and HAICCO panels).

The poster calls the collaborator an AI agent without naming its model. FAT involves a chain of associations and DAT words as different from one another as possible; forward flow measures semantic distance between pairs of words (PDF p. 1, HAICCO and HAICCO Tasks panels).
AUT and SFT each allow two minutes. AUT fluency counts responses, and originality is calculated with the LLM-based CLAUS measure (PDF p. 1, Cognitive Assessment (Pre/Post) panel).

Both forward-flow reported strings correctly describe the collaborative line as higher than the solo line at every displayed round. No numerical point estimates, test statistics, p-values, or numerical confidence limits accompany these plots (PDF p. 1, Results, Analysis of Mean).

The DAT variability statement is supported: collaborative full-chain SD is lower than solo SD. The FAT panel also displays higher collaborative SD; the poster does not define an across-person similarity metric (PDF p. 1, Results, Analysis of Standard Deviation; HAICCO Tasks).

All four AUT reported strings correctly describe higher post-HAICCO fluency and lower post-HAICCO CLAUS originality in both groups. The charts supply no printed exact outcome estimates or inferential tests, and their error bars are not defined (PDF p. 1, Results, AUT charts and caption; Conclusions).

SFT is explicitly a control semantic retrieval task. Its caption reports increased fluency in FAT and no change in semantic breadth; these control results are distinct from the AUT creativity results (PDF p. 1, HAICCO text; Cognitive Assessment; Results, lower-right SFT charts and caption).

This is an empirical poster, not a review or meta-analysis; no study-level pooled estimates, intervals, or standardizers are reported, so the default synthesis fields are appropriate (PDF p. 1, entire poster).
summary: The poster supports a nonrandomized observational design, with 100 FAT and 101 DAT completers. The form needs corrections to analysis counts, unresolved template fields, the omitted variability outcome, and wording of the evidence.
